concept.definition: Fine-tuning is the process of taking a pre-trained model and updating all its parameters on a smaller, task-specific labeled dataset to adapt it for a particular downstream task.
concept.simpleExplanation: Imagine you have a model that already understands general language patterns from reading billions of words. To make it good at a specific job—like answering questions or judging if two sentences mean the same thing—you take that pre-trained model and give it a little extra training on examples for that job. This extra training adjusts the model's internal numbers slightly so it performs well on the new task.
concept.analogy: Think of a chef who has learned to cook hundreds of dishes from around the world (pre-training). When asked to specialize in making perfect paella, they don't start from scratch; they just practice a few paella recipes with local ingredients to tweak their technique. That practice session is the fine-tuning.
concept.whyUsedHere: BERT is designed to be pre-trained once on unlabeled text and then fine-tuned separately for each downstream task (e.g., question answering, natural language inference) by adding only a small classification layer on top and updating all parameters end-to-end. This avoids building task-specific architectures from scratch and achieves state-of-the-art results with minimal changes.
